newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: COKE TO SPEND $45 MLN ON MOZAMBIQUE BUSINESS.
newsitem.headline: COKE TO SPEND $45 MLN ON MOZAMBIQUE BUSINESS.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co said on Friday it would invest $45 million to double its business in Mozambique over the next four years.
The firm made the announcement at the opening of a new Mozambique bottling plant in Chimoio -- a joint venture between Coke, Coca-Cola Sabco and the Mozambique government.
Coca-Cola Sabco, based in the South African coastal city of Port Elizabeth, is Coke's anchor bottler in Africa with operations in Namibia, Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya and South Africa.
"Mozambique is a great place to do business for any well-run, well-supported venture," said Carl Ware, Coke's Africa group president.
Coke's future investments in Mozambique, which is enjoying peace after years of bitter civil war in the aftermath of its 1975 independence from Portugal, will include a new bottling plant at Nampula.
Other projects in the country are an expansion of production at Beira and Mapouto and the establishment of a country-wide series of depots.
"We're more bullish about the opportunities in Africa than ever before," said Phil Gutsche, chief executive of Coca-Cola Sabco.
